--- title: 02 · Centrality & backbone --- **RQ1 — who is central, and where does Austria rank?** Computes degree, strength, betweenness, eigenvector centrality and PageRank on the directed weighted graph, ranks the hubs through SQL, and extracts the disparity-filter backbone. Why weighted betweenness uses `distance = 1 / value_kusd`, and why unweighted betweenness is identically zero here, is explained on the [Data & method](../data.qmd) page. ::: {#1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from __future__ import annotations import pandas as pd from IPython.display import Markdown, display from eu_trade_network import config, data_loader, db, graph, metrics, viz ``` ::: ## Graph + centralities Rebuild the edge list / digraph for `config.YEAR`, compute strengths and centralities, then refresh the DuckDB `nodes` table. ::: {#3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} edgelist = data_loader.build_edgelist() G = graph.build_graph(edgelist) summary = graph.graph_summary(G) cent = metrics.compute_centralities(G) node_meta = ( pd.DataFrame([{"iso3": n, **attrs} for n, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)]) .sort_values("iso3") .reset_index(drop=True) ) nodes_db = node_meta.merge(cent, on="iso3", how="inner") con = db.connect() db.init_schema(con) db.write_table( con, "nodes", nodes_db[ [ "iso3", "name", "grp", "out_strength", "in_strength", "degree", "betweenness", "betweenness_u", "eigenvector", "pagerank", ] ], ) # Keep edges in sync if NB01 has not been run in this environment. edges_db = edgelist.copy() edges_db["year"] = config.YEAR db.write_table(con, "edges", edges_db[["exporter_iso3", "importer_iso3", "value_kusd", "year"]]) print(summary) print(f"Updated {len(nodes_db)} nodes → {config.DB_PATH}") cent.sort_values("betweenness", ascending=False).head(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'n_nodes': 35.0, 'n_edges': 1190.0, 'density': 1.0, 'is_weakly_connected': 1.0, 'total_value_kusd': 9754928047.254004} Updated 35 nodes → /home/emilia/projects/eu-trade-network/data/processed/trade.duckdb ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} aut = hubs.loc[hubs["iso3"] == "AUT"].iloc[0] aut_pr_rank = int( hubs.sort_values("pagerank", ascending=False) .reset_index(drop=True) .assign(r=lambda d: d.index + 1) .loc[lambda d: d["iso3"] == "AUT", "r"] .iloc[0] ) aut_str_rank = int( cent.sort_values("out_strength", ascending=False) .reset_index(drop=True) .assign(r=lambda d: d.index + 1) .loc[lambda d: d["iso3"] == "AUT", "r"] .iloc[0] ) n_zero_b = int((hubs["betweenness"] == 0).sum()) n_pos_b = int((hubs["betweenness"] > 0).sum()) top_hub = hubs.iloc[0] display( Markdown( f"**{top_hub['name']} leads, and position is not volume.** " f"{top_hub['name']} ({top_hub['iso3']}) scores " f"{float(top_hub['betweenness']):.3f} on weighted betweenness. Only {n_pos_b} of " f"{len(hubs)} economies score above zero at all, because the digraph is complete " f"(density = {summary['density']:.2f}): for most pairs the direct link is already " f"the cheapest path, so nobody sits between them.\n\n" f"**Austria is not a bridge.** It is one of the {n_zero_b} economies with " f"betweenness = 0 — the SQL rank of {int(aut['rank'])} is an arbitrary tie-break " f"among those zeros, not a ranking. Its partners already trade with each other " f"directly. By export strength Austria is {aut_str_rank}th of {len(hubs)} and by " f"PageRank {aut_pr_rank}th: a mid-tier EU economy whose largest partner is Germany " f"on both sides of the trade balance." ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Germany leads, and position is not volume.** Germany (DEU) scores 0.829 on weighted betweenness. Only 15 of 35 economies score above zero at all, because the digraph is complete (density = 1.00): for most pairs the direct link is already the cheapest path, so nobody sits between them. **Austria is not a bridge.** It is one of the 20 economies with betweenness = 0 — the SQL rank of 35 is an arbitrary tie-break among those zeros, not a ranking. Its partners already trade with each other directly. By export strength Austria is 17th of 35 and by PageRank 13th: a mid-tier EU economy whose largest partner is Germany on both sides of the trade balance. ::: ::: ## Strength distribution The network is dense (near-complete bilateral coverage). We plot the strength ranking and **do not** fit a power law. ::: {#9 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig_strength = viz.plot_degree_distribution(cent) fig_strength.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Disparity-filter backbone Statistically significant edges at `config.DISPARITY_ALPHA` (Serrano, Boguñá & Vespignani 2009). Also compute the rich-club coefficient on the undirected projection. ::: {#11 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} backbone = metrics.disparity_filter(G, alpha=config.DISPARITY_ALPHA) bb_edges = pd.DataFrame( [ {"exporter_iso3": u, "importer_iso3": v, "value_kusd": float(d["weight"])} for u, v, d in backbone.edges(data=True) ] ) rc = metrics.rich_club(G) print( f"Backbone keeps {backbone.number_of_edges()} / {G.number_of_edges()} edges " f"at alpha={config.DISPARITY_ALPHA}" ) rc.tail(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Backbone keeps 184 / 1190 edges at alpha=0.05 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
